cues.en: It's worse with every generation. For some reason, it just keeps getting worse. I'll give you an example of that. There's a condition in combat.
cues.zh: 每一代都更糟。不知为何，它就是越来越糟。我给大家举个例子。战场上有一种病症。

cues.en: Most people know about it. It's when a fighting person's nervous system has been stressed to its absolute peak and maximum, can't take any more input. The nervous system has either snapped or is about to snap.
cues.zh: 大多数人都知道它。它指的是，作战人员的神经系统被压到极限，再也承受不了任何刺激。这时神经系统要么已经崩溃，要么濒临崩溃。

cues.en: In the first world war, that condition was called shell shock.
cues.zh: 第一次世界大战时，这种情况被称为弹震症。

cues.en: Simple,
cues.zh: 简单，

cues.en: honest, direct language,
cues.zh: 坦诚、直接的语言，

cues.en: two syllables,
cues.zh: 两个音节，

cues.en: shell shock.
cues.zh: 炮弹休克。

cues.en: Almost sounds like the guns themselves.
cues.zh: 听起来几乎就像枪炮本身。

cues.en: That was seventy years ago.
cues.zh: 那是七十年前的事了。

cues.en: Then a whole generation went by, and the second world war came along and we... The very same combat condition was called battle fatigue.
cues.zh: 然后整整一代人过去了，第二次世界大战到来，我们……同一种战斗病症被叫作战斗疲劳症。

cues.en: Four syllables now. Takes a little longer to say.
cues.zh: 现在四个音节了。说起来要稍微久一点。

cues.en: Doesn't seem to hurt as much.
cues.zh: 似乎就没那么痛了。

cues.en: Fatigue is a nicer word than shock. Shell shock. Battle fatigue.
cues.zh: “疲劳”比“休克”好听。炮弹休克。战斗疲劳。

cues.en: Then
cues.zh: 后来

cues.en: we had the war in Korea in 1950.
cues.zh: 1950年，我们打了朝鲜战争。

cues.en: Madison Avenue was riding high by that time, and the very same combat condition
cues.zh: 那时麦迪逊大道正风光无限，而同一种作战状况

cues.en: was called operational
cues.zh: 被称为“作战性”

cues.en: exhaustion.
cues.zh: 衰竭。

cues.en: Hey, we're up to eight syllables now.
cues.zh: 嘿，现在都八个音节了。

cues.en: And the humanity has been squeezed completely out of the phrase. It's totally sterile now.
cues.zh: 这个词组里的人情味被彻底挤没了。现在完全干巴巴的。

cues.en: Operational exhaustion
cues.zh: 作战性衰竭

cues.en: sounds like something that might happen to your car.
cues.zh: 听起来像是你车上会出的毛病。

cues.en: Then, of course, came the war in Vietnam,
cues.zh: 然后当然是越南战争，

cues.en: which has only been over for about sixteen or seventeen years. And thanks to the lies and deceit surrounding that war, I guess it's no surprise that the very same condition
cues.zh: 那场战争结束才不过大约十六七年。多亏围绕那场战争的谎言和欺骗，我想，同样的状况

cues.en: was called post traumatic stress disorder.
cues.zh: 被称为创伤后应激障碍。

cues.en: Still eight syllables, but we've added a hyphen.
cues.zh: 还是八个音节，但我们加了个连字符。

cues.en: And the pain is completely buried under jargon.
cues.zh: 而痛苦被完全埋在术语下面。

cues.en: Post traumatic stress disorder.
cues.zh: 创伤后应激障碍。

cues.en: I'll bet you if we'd have still been calling it shell shock, some of those Vietnam veterans might have gotten the attention they needed at the time. I'll bet you.
cues.zh: 我敢打赌，如果我们还叫它“弹震症”，那些越战老兵里有些人当时可能就得到了需要的关注。我敢打赌。

cues.en: I'll bet you.
cues.zh: 我敢打赌。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: but it didn't happen. And one of the reasons one of the reasons is because we were using that soft language,
cues.zh: 但事情没有发生。原因之一，原因之一，就是我们用了那种软绵绵的语言，

cues.en: that language that takes the life out of life. And it is a function of time. It does keep getting worse. Give you another example. Sometime during my life, sometime during my life, toilet paper became bathroom tissue. I
cues.zh: 那种把生命中的生气抽走的语言。而且它是时间的函数。它确实一直在变糟。再给你举个例子。在我有生之年，在我有生之年，厕纸变成了卫生间纸巾。我

cues.en: wasn't notified of this.
cues.zh: 没人通知我这件事。

cues.en: No one asked me if I agreed with it. It just happened. Toilet paper became bathroom tissue.
cues.zh: 没人问过我是否同意。它就是发生了。厕纸变成了卫生纸。

cues.en: Sneakers became running shoes.
cues.zh: 运动鞋变成了跑鞋。

cues.en: False teeth became dental appliances.
cues.zh: 假牙变成了牙科器具。

cues.en: Medicine
cues.zh: 药

cues.en: became medication.
cues.zh: 变成了药物。

cues.en: Information
cues.zh: 信息

cues.en: became directory assistance.
cues.zh: 变成了查号服务。

cues.en: The dump became the landfill.
cues.zh: 垃圾场变成了填埋场。

cues.en: Car crashes became automobile accidents.
cues.zh: 撞车变成了交通事故。

cues.en: Partly cloudy became partly sunny.
cues.zh: 局部多云变成了局部晴朗。

cues.en: Motels became motor lodges.
cues.zh: 汽车旅馆变成了汽车旅舍。

cues.en: House trailers became mobile homes.
cues.zh: 拖车房变成了移动房屋。

cues.en: Used cars became previously owned transportation.
cues.zh: 二手车变成了“前车主用过的交通工具”。

cues.en: Room service became guest room dining,
cues.zh: 客房送餐服务变成了客房内用餐，

cues.en: and constipation became occasional irregularity.
cues.zh: 便秘变成了偶发性排便不规律。

cues.en: When I was a little kid, if I got sick, wanted me to go to the hospital and see the doctor. Now they want me to go to a health maintenance organization
cues.zh: 我小时候，如果我生病了，他们想让我去医院看医生。现在他们想让我去健康维护组织

cues.en: or a wellness center to consult a health care delivery professional.
cues.zh: 或者去健康中心咨询医疗保健服务专业人员。

cues.en: Poor people used to live in slums.
cues.zh: 穷人过去住在贫民窟。

cues.en: Now the economically disadvantaged occupies substandard housing in the inner cities.
cues.zh: 现在经济弱势群体住在内城区的劣质住房里。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: they're broke.
cues.zh: 他们没钱了。

cues.en: They're broke. They don't have a negative cash flow position.
cues.zh: 他们没钱了。他们的现金流并不是负的。

cues.en: They're fucking broke.
cues.zh: 他们他妈的就是没钱了。

cues.en: Because a lot of them were fired. You know fired? Management wanted to curtail redundancies in the human resources area,
cues.zh: 因为很多人被解雇了。你知道解雇吗？管理层想减少人力资源领域的冗员，

cues.en: so many people are no longer viable members of the workforce.
cues.zh: 于是很多人不再是劳动力队伍中的有效成员。

cues.en: Smug,
cues.zh: 自鸣得意，

cues.en: greedy,
cues.zh: 贪婪，

cues.en: well fed white people have invented a language to conceal their sins. It's as simple as that. The CIA doesn't kill anybody anymore. They neutralize
cues.zh: 养尊处优的白人发明了一种语言来掩盖自己的罪过。就这么简单。CIA 不再杀任何人了。他们“中和”

cues.en: people
cues.zh: 人

cues.en: or they depopulate
cues.zh: 或者他们清空

cues.en: the area.
cues.zh: 这个地区。

cues.en: The government doesn't lie and engages in disinformation.
cues.zh: 政府不说谎，他们搞的是虚假信息。

cues.en: The Pentagon actually measures nuclear radiation in something they call
cues.zh: 五角大楼实际上测量核辐射，用的单位他们叫

cues.en: sunshine units.
cues.zh: 阳光单位。

cues.en: Israeli murderers are called commandos.
cues.zh: 以色列的杀人犯被称为突击队员。

cues.en: Arab commandos are called terrorists.
cues.zh: 阿拉伯突击队员被称为恐怖分子。

cues.en: Contra killers are called freedom fighters.
cues.zh: Contra 的杀人者被称为自由战士。

cues.en: Well, if crime fighters fight crime and firefighters fight fire, what do freedom fighters fight? They
cues.zh: 那么，如果犯罪斗士打击犯罪、消防员扑灭火灾，那自由战士打击什么？他们

cues.en: never mention that part of it to us, do they?
cues.zh: 从来不跟我们提这一部分，对吧？

cues.en: Never mention that part of it. And...
cues.zh: 永远别提那部分。还有……

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: And some of this stuff is just silly. We know. We all know that. Like on the airlines, they say they want to pre board. Well, what the hell is pre board? What does that mean? To get on before you get on?
cues.zh: 而且有些东西就是很蠢。我们知道。我们都清楚。比如航空公司，他们说要“预登机”。预登机到底是什么鬼？那是什么意思？先登机再登机？

cues.en: They say they're going to pre board those passengers in need of special assistance.
cues.zh: 他们说要让需要特殊协助的乘客预登机。

cues.en: Cripples.
cues.zh: 瘸子。

cues.en: Simple,
cues.zh: 简单，

cues.en: honest, direct language.
cues.zh: 诚实、直接的语言。

cues.en: There's no shame attached to the word cripple that I can find in any dictionary. No shame attached to it. In fact, it's a word used in bible translations. Jesus healed the cripples. Doesn't take seven words to describe that condition.
cues.zh: 我翻遍任何词典，都找不到“瘸子”这个词带有羞耻含义。它不带羞耻。事实上，圣经译本就用这个词。耶稣治好了瘸子。描述那种状况不需要七个词。

cues.en: But we don't have any cripples in this country anymore.
cues.zh: 这个国家再也没有瘸子了。

cues.en: We have
cues.zh: 我们有

cues.en: the physically challenged.
cues.zh: 身体受挑战者。

cues.en: Is that a grotesque enough evasion for you? How
cues.zh: 这种回避对你来说够不够荒诞？那

cues.en: about differently abled?
cues.zh: 叫“不同能力者”怎么样？

cues.en: I've heard them call that differently abled.
cues.zh: 我听过他们管那叫“不同能力者”。

cues.en: You can't even call these people handicapped anymore. They'll say, we're not handicapped.
cues.zh: 现在你连“残疾人”都不能叫了。他们会说，我们不是残疾人。

cues.en: We're handicape
cues.zh: 我们是残障

cues.en: able.
cues.zh: 能者。

cues.en: These poor people have been bullshitted by the system into believing that if you change the name of the condition, somehow you'll change the condition. Well, hey cousin.
cues.zh: 这些可怜人被这套话术忽悠了，以为只要改掉状况的名字，就能以某种方式改变状况。好吧，老兄。

cues.en: Doesn't happen.
cues.zh: 不会发生。

cues.en: Doesn't happen.
cues.zh: 不会发生。

cues.en: We have no more deaf people in this country, hearing impaired.
cues.zh: 这个国家再也没有聋人了，只有听障人士。

cues.en: No one's blind anymore, partially sighted or visually impaired.
cues.zh: 再也没有盲人了，只有低视力者或视障者。

cues.en: We have no more stupid people. Everybody has a learning disorder.
cues.zh: 我们再也没有蠢人了。每个人都有学习障碍。

cues.en: Or he's minimally exceptional.
cues.zh: 或者他只是“轻度特殊”。

cues.en: How would you like to be told that about your child?
cues.zh: 如果别人这样评价你的孩子，你愿意听吗？

cues.en: He's minimally exceptional.
cues.zh: 他是“轻度特殊”。

cues.en: Oh, thank god for that.
cues.zh: 哦，谢天谢地。

cues.en: Psychologists actually have started calling ugly people those with severe appearance deficits. Deficits.
cues.zh: 心理学家其实已经开始把丑人叫作“有严重外貌缺陷的人”。缺陷。

cues.en: It's getting so bad that any day now I expect to hear a rape victim referred to as an unwilling sperm recipient.
cues.zh: 情况越来越糟，我估计随时都会听到强奸受害者被称为不情愿的精子接收者。

cues.en: And we have no more old people in this country. No more old people. We shipped them all away,
cues.zh: 这个国家已经没有老人了。没有老人了。我们把他们全送走了，

cues.en: and we brought in these
cues.zh: 然后我们引进了这些

cues.en: senior
cues.zh: 老年

cues.en: citizens.
cues.zh: 公民。

cues.en: Isn't that a typically American
cues.zh: 这不就是典型的美国

cues.en: twentieth century phrase?
cues.zh: 二十世纪的说法吗？

cues.en: Bloodless,
cues.zh: 毫无血色，

cues.en: lifeless.
cues.zh: 毫无生气。

cues.en: No pulse in one of them.
cues.zh: 里面一点脉搏都没有。

cues.en: A senior citizen.
cues.zh: 一个老年公民。

cues.en: But I've accepted that one. I've come to terms with it. I know it's here to stay. We'll never get rid of it. That's what they're gonna be called, so I'll relax on that. But the one I do resist, the one I keep resisting is when they look at an old guy and they'll say, look at him, Dan. He's 90 years young.
cues.zh: 但这个词我接受了。我已经想通了。我知道它会一直存在。我们永远摆脱不了它。他们以后就会这么叫，所以这点我不计较了。但我真正抗拒的、一直抗拒的，是当他们看着一个老头说：看看他，Dan。他90岁还年轻着呢。

cues.en: Imagine the fear of aging that reveals,
cues.zh: 想象一下，这种对衰老的恐惧揭示出什么，

cues.en: to not even be able to use the word old to describe someone, to have to use an antonym.
cues.zh: 甚至不能用“老”这个词来形容一个人，只能改用反义词。

cues.en: And fear of aging is natural. It's universal, isn't it? We all have that. No one wants to get old. No one wants to die, but we do.
cues.zh: 对衰老的恐惧是自然的。它普遍存在，不是吗？我们都有。没人想变老。没人想死，但我们终将死去。

cues.en: So we bullshit ourselves.
cues.zh: 所以我们自欺欺人。

cues.en: I started bullshitting myself when I got to my forties. Soon as I was in my forties, I'd look in the mirror and I'd say,
cues.zh: 我四十多岁时开始自欺欺人。一到四十多岁，我照镜子就会说：

cues.en: well, I I guess I'm getting
cues.zh: 嗯，我，我猜我正变得

cues.en: older.
cues.zh: 更老了。

cues.en: Older sounds a little better than old, doesn't it? Sounds like it might even last a little longer.
cues.zh: “年长”听起来比“老”好一点，对吧？听起来甚至还能多撑一阵。

cues.en: Bullshit. I'm getting old.
cues.zh: 扯淡。我是在变老。

cues.en: And it's okay.
cues.zh: 这也没关系。

cues.en: Because thanks to our fear of death in this country, I won't have to die. I'll
cues.zh: 因为在我们这个国家，多亏了对死亡的恐惧，我不用死。我会

cues.en: pass away.
cues.zh: 去世。

cues.en: Or I'll expire like a magazine subscription.
cues.zh: 或者像杂志订阅一样到期。

cues.en: If it happens in the hospital, they'll call it a terminal episode.
cues.zh: 如果发生在医院，他们会叫它“临终事件”。

cues.en: The insurance company will refer to it as negative patient care outcome.
cues.zh: 保险公司会称其为“患者护理负面结果”。

cues.en: And if it's the result of malpractice, they'll say it was a therapeutic misadventure.
cues.zh: 如果这是医疗失当造成的，他们就会说那是一次“治疗性意外”。

cues.en: I'm telling you, some of this language makes me wanna vomit.
cues.zh: 我跟你说，有些这种说法让我想吐。

cues.en: Well, maybe not vomit.
cues.zh: 好吧，也许还不至于吐。

cues.en: Makes me want to engage in an involuntary personal protein spill.
cues.zh: 让我想来一次非自愿的个人蛋白质溢出。
